card.title: Down's process — why sodium needs electricity, not carbon

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Extraction follows reactivity: carbon reduces middle ores (roasted sulphides, calcined carbonates), while Na/Al sit above carbon in the series — only electrolysis (electrometallurgy) rips them free. Down's cell electrolyses fused NaCl (with CaCl₂ to lower the melt point); cathode: Na⁺ + e⁻ → Na, anode: 2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2e⁻. Refining (poling, electrorefining) then purifies; flux/slag chemistry floats gangue away.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: reactivity ladder decides: K Na Ca Mg Al | (C) | Zn Fe | Sn Pb | (H) | Cu Ag Au — above C: electrolysis only  ·  Down's: 2NaCl(fused) → 2Na + Cl₂ (cathode steel, anode graphite)  ·  carbon reduction: MO + C → M + CO (middle metals)  ·  thermite: Fe₂O₃ + 2Al → 2Fe + Al₂O₃

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Down's needs FUSED (molten) NaCl — aqueous solution would discharge H₂ instead (water reduces more easily than Na⁺). Carbon reduction needs the oxide below carbon's line on the Ellingham diagram at furnace T. Roasting (sulphides, in air) vs calcination (carbonates, no air) split by ore type.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Aluminium ignores carbon for the same reason — Hall-Héroult electrolyses alumina in cryolite instead (NEB 2022). Sodium explodes in water (H₂ + heat), forms peroxide with excess O₂, and gives blue solutions in liquid ammonia (solvated electrons). Bleaching powder = CaOCl₂, plaster of Paris = CaSO₄·½H₂O, Epsom = MgSO₄·7H₂O.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Why not carbon for aluminium? Al sits above carbon in the reactivity series — carbon cannot reduce Al₂O₃ (ΔG positive); only electrolysis works: dissolve alumina in molten cryolite, electrolyse → Al at cathode, CO/CO₂ at the graphite anode (NEB 2022, 3-mark pattern, mirrored by the Down's 5-marker).

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Reactivity-series order is for standard aqueous conditions — high-T Ellingham crossings (e.g. Mg reducing others) break the ladder. Electrolysis is energy-hungry (aluminium's cost is electricity). Bauxite impurities demand Bayer refining before Hall-Héroult even starts.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Down's cell logic: melt NaCl → mobile Na⁺/Cl⁻; apply potential above decomposition voltage; cathode reduces Na⁺ (liquid Na floats, collected), anode oxidises Cl⁻ (Cl₂ piped off). CaCl₂/CaF₂ addition lowers mp from 801 °C toward ~600 °C — less heat, less Na vaporisation loss. Sodium's violent water reaction (2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂) proves its series position.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: 'Explain extraction of X' → locate X vs carbon: above → electrolysis (name the cell + electrodes + reactions), middle → roast/calcine + carbon, below → heat alone. Down's 5-marker: cell + why fused + CaCl₂ role + both electrode reactions.

rows.label: Board question
